_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); cruise-line signals

pit_profile.why: Royal Caribbean: 'We are the world’s second largest cruise company operating 40 ships in the cruise vacation industry with an aggregate of approximately 92,300 berths as of December 31, 2010'; 'We compete principally on the basis of innovation and quality of ships, quality of service, variety of itineraries, choice of destinations and price'; 'We may lose business to competitors throughout the vacation market'; and 'The demand for cruises is affected by international, national and local economic and business conditions and is sensitive to reductions in discretionary consumer spending' (its own FY2010 10-K): a cruise-fleet franchise whose demand follows the economies it sells into, by its own account; no disruption theme is live for it

classification.quality_note: Royal Caribbean: 'We are the world’s second largest cruise company operating 40 ships in the cruise vacation industry with an aggregate of approximately 92,300 berths as of December 31, 2010'; 'We compete principally on the basis of innovation and quality of ships, quality of service, variety of itineraries, choice of destinations and price'; 'We may lose business to competitors throughout the vacation market'; and 'The demand for cruises is affected by international, national and local economic and business conditions and is sensitive to reductions in discretionary consumer spending' (its own FY2010 10-K): a cruise-fleet franchise whose demand follows the economies it sells into, by its own account; no disruption theme is live for it. durable franchise (obsolescence risk 2/5); price cheap; Ratio B 0.62x; -4% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap +1.37; conservative 2yr +104%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -73.5%/yr (worst year FY01-FY10, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +7.1%/yr (Q3 cc guide + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +7.1%/yr (FY01-FY10 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +46.1%/yr (best 2-yr run FY01-FY10); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: RCL (retrospective, 2011-08-19) ◉ BUY — Ratio B 0.62x (91.1% downside to Bear $2 / +146.0% upside to Bull $55) | Adj composite 2.97 vs market 1.60: gap +1.37 [UNDERVALUED] | -4% above the EPP floor $23 (8x FY11E $2.90) | Conservative 2-yr case: +104.1% total (+52.1%/yr) | At 7.7x FY11E the 15% hurdle price $30 sits at or below the BASE case; Net Yields +3.8% in Q2 2011, forward net revenue +7.36-8.43% (Q3 2011 net revenue guide at constant currency); no disruption theme has dated evidence.
